approach.method_basis: The Parent starts at the best supplied scored molecule and repeatedly samples local atom, bond, path and ring edits from that one current graph. It sanitizes and normalizes each edited molecular identity, rejects previously proposed molecules, and submits the first full batch admitted by short-term inverse-motif memory. Memory vetoes a neighbor only when both inverse signs match the same earlier selected transition. The highest-scoring accepted neighbor becomes the next current graph even when its score worsens, while a separate archive keeps the best observation. Bounded inverse restrictions, four-step aging, overlap refresh and obstruction release remain part of that Parent, as does the repaired proposal-to-feedback identity join.
approach.novelty: Add one local sulfur-valence introduction gate. A generated neighbor may retain or remove a sulfur environment already present in its source, but it may not introduce or multiply a sulfur environment outside an explicit small envelope of ordinary valence patterns. This redirects eligible graph edits toward alternative neighbors before they reach the unchanged memory gate. It preserves thiol and sulfide valence, aromatic sulfur, terminal carbon-sulfur double bonds, and the usual neutral sulfur-oxide patterns. Earlier siblings changed memory matching and repaired identity bookkeeping; they did not constrain sulfur chemistry. The related corpus-support experiment in another walk admitted chemistry merely because it occurred locally in a corpus. This proposal instead tests a fixed, narrow sulfur rule without learning a vocabulary or changing preparation.

hypothesis: Reject an otherwise valid canonically novel graph neighbor before tabu testing exactly when it introduces or increases the multiplicity of a sulfur local-environment signature outside a fixed neutral sulfur-valence envelope relative to the same scored source graph, then continue the inherited graph-edit sampling loop from that unchanged source.

finding_summary.headline: The sulfur gate eliminated targeted violations, with higher sampling cost and uneven score gains.
finding_summary.insights:
The targeted sulfur channel was largely independent of the existing tabu veto: 760 of 766 rejected draws would otherwise have reached allocation. Ordinary sulfur alternatives remain abundant enough to fill every batch and retain the panel's average score, despite the extra sampling work. All selected initial sources were already clean under the envelope, so the experiment demonstrates prevention of new violations; it does not exercise recovery from an inherited violating source. Most rejected opportunities come from atom replacement, which accounts for 734 of the 766 rejections.

The small favorable mean score is accompanied by a substantial loss in one seed and lower mean scores on two tasks. It supports the stated mean non-inferiority direction on this panel without establishing a consistent improvement. The molecular assessment also shows where the chemical benefit stops: more ordinary sulfur and recognizable aromatic polyamines coexist with nitrogen/oxygen-halogen bonds, constrained unsaturation, dense cages and unspecified stereochemistry. Sulfur valence is one separable source of implausible chemistry; whole-molecule stability, accessible ring geometry and stereochemistry remain unresolved.
finding_summary.results:
The gate rejected 766 of 5,307 otherwise valid novel neighbors across all fifteen task sessions. Of those rejections, 760 would have passed the unchanged tabu rule, and every rejection was followed by a different permitted neighbor from the same scored source. None of the 4,350 emitted molecules contains sulfur outside the declared envelope, compared with 2,398 of 4,350 Parent emissions. Sulfur remains in 2,821 emitted molecules, including thiols, sulfides, aromatic sulfur, thiones, sulfoxides and sulfones.

All three seeds complete all five 300-evaluation tasks and all 435 ten-member batches. The sampling cost rises from 5,285 to 6,234 raw attempts, or 12.15 to 14.33 attempts per batch. Emission yield falls from 82.31% to 69.78% of raw attempts. Recorded edits, normalized identities, accepted-score joins and downstream memory/winner rules pass the independent audit.

Mean macro final Top-1 rises from 0.520918 to 0.526783, a paired mean change of +0.005865. The seed changes are +0.015565, -0.061423 and +0.063454, and the macro population standard deviation rises from 0.004890 to 0.046774. Zaleplon and median_2 improve in every matched seed; decoration hopping declines in every seed, while DRD2 and sitagliptin have mixed outcomes. The gate therefore achieves its intended chemical and allocation changes with an uneven score response.

molecular.headline: More conventional sulfur and amine skeletons coexist with N-halogen bonds, hypobromites and severely strained cages
molecular.overall_character: The current three-seed panel contains 900 recorded entries and 870 optimizer proposals per task, compared with the supplied three-seed Parent n-9f7c7ec50039 trajectories. Ring-closure and branch presence rates are 1.0 throughout; aromatic-token presence ranges from 0.9379 to 1.0, and charge and stereocentre token presence remain 0.0. These are string-presence counters, not atom fractions or measurements of ionization and stereochemical feasibility. The prominent high-scoring sulfur motifs now include thiols, sulfides, thiones, sulfoxides and aromatic sulfur, rather than the Parent's frequently multiply bonded hydrogen-bearing sulfur cages. Some aromatic amine leaders are entirely sulfur-free and have substantially more recognizable medicinal skeletons. This is a real difference in the observed chemistry, but the output still includes reactive N-Br/N-Cl/N-F and O-Br bonds, N-N/N-O networks, highly constrained small rings and dense carbon/nitrogen cages. Aromatic ring/carbonyl families, large decorated diones and polycyclic amines give moderate diversity across tasks and seeds; local families dominate each late trajectory. Overall synthetic plausibility remains poor because several of the leading complete structures are severely strained or reactive, despite more plausible subseries. No activation or causal attribution is inferred from these molecular observations.

per_task.generated_character: Moderately sized aromatic/fused-ring carbonyl compounds remain prominent. Seed 2 reaches a methoxy- and methyl-substituted indene linked to pyridine through a carbonyl-S-N unit carrying N-Br. These replace the Parent's unusual-sulfur ketones or N-chloroamides with different sulfur chemistry, but several leaders still combine reactive functionalities. The aryl ketone subseries is comparatively plausible.

N-N/N-O networks and constrained unsaturated ring closures remain chemically or geometrically questionable.
missing_features: Broader stable realizations of the compact aryl-carbonyl arrangement are underrepresented relative to N-halogen, sulfenamide and hydrazine substitutions.

method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.

applicability_conditions: The current Parent has complete formal evidence and exercised sulfur-introduction opportunities in every saved session; this removes the earlier identity failure as an explanation of the targeted chemical channel. The sulfur envelope is an explicit narrow search constraint, not a learned chemistry distribution or a universal list of chemically valid sulfur compounds. It excludes charged sulfur and some rare valid motifs while retaining potentially reactive single-bonded sulfur species. It does not constrain N-halogen bonds, ring strain, global functional-group compatibility or stereochemistry.

Source-relative signature multiplicities permit existing outside-envelope chemistry only without introducing or multiplying an outside-envelope signature. Starting states remain those chosen by the inherited accepted-score rule. A changed disallowed environment is a new signature even when the total number of disallowed sulfur centers does not rise.

Enough zero-D, canonically novel, tabu-admissible neighbors must remain to fill the announced batches through the existing operators. The gate must never relax itself or change a protocol setting to escape obstruction; generation cost and completion are part of the reported evidence.

Useful score retention requires available permitted alternatives to retain productive molecular arrangements. Existing high-scoring unusual sulfur proves that a chemically motivated gate may sacrifice the benchmark score. Three matched replicas can test the supplied comparison, but the gate-only counterfactual supplies no score for excluded structures.

All non-active Layer interfaces remain frozen. The implementation adds no motif-based memory rule, winner preference, source restart, corpus vocabulary, surrogate model or objective-specific chemistry.

finding_summary.headline: The sulfur gate eliminated targeted violations, with higher sampling cost and uneven score gains.
finding_summary.insights:
The targeted sulfur channel was largely independent of the existing tabu veto: 760 of 766 rejected draws would otherwise have reached allocation. Ordinary sulfur alternatives remain abundant enough to fill every batch and retain the panel's average score, despite the extra sampling work. All selected initial sources were already clean under the envelope, so the experiment demonstrates prevention of new violations; it does not exercise recovery from an inherited violating source. Most rejected opportunities come from atom replacement, which accounts for 734 of the 766 rejections.

The small favorable mean score is accompanied by a substantial loss in one seed and lower mean scores on two tasks. It supports the stated mean non-inferiority direction on this panel without establishing a consistent improvement. The molecular assessment also shows where the chemical benefit stops: more ordinary sulfur and recognizable aromatic polyamines coexist with nitrogen/oxygen-halogen bonds, constrained unsaturation, dense cages and unspecified stereochemistry. Sulfur valence is one separable source of implausible chemistry; whole-molecule stability, accessible ring geometry and stereochemistry remain unresolved.

finding_summary.headline: The sulfur gate eliminated targeted violations, with higher sampling cost and uneven score gains.
finding_summary.insights:
The targeted sulfur channel was largely independent of the existing tabu veto: 760 of 766 rejected draws would otherwise have reached allocation. Ordinary sulfur alternatives remain abundant enough to fill every batch and retain the panel's average score, despite the extra sampling work. All selected initial sources were already clean under the envelope, so the experiment demonstrates prevention of new violations; it does not exercise recovery from an inherited violating source. Most rejected opportunities come from atom replacement, which accounts for 734 of the 766 rejections.

The small favorable mean score is accompanied by a substantial loss in one seed and lower mean scores on two tasks. It supports the stated mean non-inferiority direction on this panel without establishing a consistent improvement. The molecular assessment also shows where the chemical benefit stops: more ordinary sulfur and recognizable aromatic polyamines coexist with nitrogen/oxygen-halogen bonds, constrained unsaturation, dense cages and unspecified stereochemistry. Sulfur valence is one separable source of implausible chemistry; whole-molecule stability, accessible ring geometry and stereochemistry remain unresolved.
finding_summary.results:
The gate rejected 766 of 5,307 otherwise valid novel neighbors across all fifteen task sessions. Of those rejections, 760 would have passed the unchanged tabu rule, and every rejection was followed by a different permitted neighbor from the same scored source. None of the 4,350 emitted molecules contains sulfur outside the declared envelope, compared with 2,398 of 4,350 Parent emissions. Sulfur remains in 2,821 emitted molecules, including thiols, sulfides, aromatic sulfur, thiones, sulfoxides and sulfones.

All three seeds complete all five 300-evaluation tasks and all 435 ten-member batches. The sampling cost rises from 5,285 to 6,234 raw attempts, or 12.15 to 14.33 attempts per batch. Emission yield falls from 82.31% to 69.78% of raw attempts. Recorded edits, normalized identities, accepted-score joins and downstream memory/winner rules pass the independent audit.

Mean macro final Top-1 rises from 0.520918 to 0.526783, a paired mean change of +0.005865. The seed changes are +0.015565, -0.061423 and +0.063454, and the macro population standard deviation rises from 0.004890 to 0.046774. Zaleplon and median_2 improve in every matched seed; decoration hopping declines in every seed, while DRD2 and sitagliptin have mixed outcomes. The gate therefore achieves its intended chemical and allocation changes with an uneven score response.

finding_summary.headline: The sulfur gate eliminated targeted violations, with higher sampling cost and uneven score gains.
finding_summary.insights:
The targeted sulfur channel was largely independent of the existing tabu veto: 760 of 766 rejected draws would otherwise have reached allocation. Ordinary sulfur alternatives remain abundant enough to fill every batch and retain the panel's average score, despite the extra sampling work. All selected initial sources were already clean under the envelope, so the experiment demonstrates prevention of new violations; it does not exercise recovery from an inherited violating source. Most rejected opportunities come from atom replacement, which accounts for 734 of the 766 rejections.

The small favorable mean score is accompanied by a substantial loss in one seed and lower mean scores on two tasks. It supports the stated mean non-inferiority direction on this panel without establishing a consistent improvement. The molecular assessment also shows where the chemical benefit stops: more ordinary sulfur and recognizable aromatic polyamines coexist with nitrogen/oxygen-halogen bonds, constrained unsaturation, dense cages and unspecified stereochemistry. Sulfur valence is one separable source of implausible chemistry; whole-molecule stability, accessible ring geometry and stereochemistry remain unresolved.

molecular_assessment.headline: More conventional sulfur and amine skeletons coexist with N-halogen bonds, hypobromites and severely strained cages
molecular_assessment.overall_character: The current three-seed panel contains 900 recorded entries and 870 optimizer proposals per task, compared with the supplied three-seed Parent n-9f7c7ec50039 trajectories. Ring-closure and branch presence rates are 1.0 throughout; aromatic-token presence ranges from 0.9379 to 1.0, and charge and stereocentre token presence remain 0.0. These are string-presence counters, not atom fractions or measurements of ionization and stereochemical feasibility. The prominent high-scoring sulfur motifs now include thiols, sulfides, thiones, sulfoxides and aromatic sulfur, rather than the Parent's frequently multiply bonded hydrogen-bearing sulfur cages. Some aromatic amine leaders are entirely sulfur-free and have substantially more recognizable medicinal skeletons. This is a real difference in the observed chemistry, but the output still includes reactive N-Br/N-Cl/N-F and O-Br bonds, N-N/N-O networks, highly constrained small rings and dense carbon/nitrogen cages. Aromatic ring/carbonyl families, large decorated diones and polycyclic amines give moderate diversity across tasks and seeds; local families dominate each late trajectory. Overall synthetic plausibility remains poor because several of the leading complete structures are severely strained or reactive, despite more plausible subseries. No activation or causal attribution is inferred from these molecular observations.

per_task.generated_character: Moderately sized aromatic/fused-ring carbonyl compounds remain prominent. Seed 2 reaches a methoxy- and methyl-substituted indene linked to pyridine through a carbonyl-S-N unit carrying N-Br. Seed 1 contains more conventional indene aryl ketones with ethylthio, methylamino and methoxy substituents; other high examples carry hydrazine, bromomethoxy or sulfenamide groups. Seed 0 reaches an N-bromothioamide on an oxygen-containing unsaturated fused framework. Aromatic-token presence is 0.9977 and halogen presence is 0.8402. These replace the Parent's unusual-sulfur ketones or N-chloroamides with different sulfur chemistry, but several leaders still combine reactive functionalities. The aryl ketone subseries is comparatively plausible.
liabilities: Acyl-S-N-Br, N-bromothioamide and bromomethoxy groups introduce substantial reactivity despite ordinary sulfur valence.
N-N/N-O networks and constrained unsaturated ring closures remain chemically or geometrically questionable.
missing_features: Broader stable realizations of the compact aryl-carbonyl arrangement are underrepresented relative to N-halogen, sulfenamide and hydrazine substitutions.

Accessible alternatives to the late bridged N-O frameworks and explicit configurations for products that acquire stereocentres are absent from the shown high/final series; no unique target-specific group is established.

approach.method_basis: The Parent starts at the best supplied scored molecule and repeatedly samples local atom, bond, path and ring edits from that one current graph. It sanitizes and normalizes each edited molecular identity, rejects previously proposed molecules, and submits the first full batch admitted by short-term inverse-motif memory. Memory vetoes a neighbor only when both inverse signs match the same earlier selected transition. The highest-scoring accepted neighbor becomes the next current graph even when its score worsens, while a separate archive keeps the best observation. Bounded inverse restrictions, four-step aging, overlap refresh and obstruction release remain part of that Parent, as does the repaired proposal-to-feedback identity join.
approach.novelty: Add one local sulfur-valence introduction gate. A generated neighbor may retain or remove a sulfur environment already present in its source, but it may not introduce or multiply a sulfur environment outside an explicit small envelope of ordinary valence patterns. This redirects eligible graph edits toward alternative neighbors before they reach the unchanged memory gate. It preserves thiol and sulfide valence, aromatic sulfur, terminal carbon-sulfur double bonds, and the usual neutral sulfur-oxide patterns. Earlier siblings changed memory matching and repaired identity bookkeeping; they did not constrain sulfur chemistry. The related corpus-support experiment in another walk admitted chemistry merely because it occurred locally in a corpus. This proposal instead tests a fixed, narrow sulfur rule without learning a vocabulary or changing preparation.
